thread: Follow the weather upward: begin at a mountain observatory, trace the atmosphere through a global network of instruments, and look back at Earth from weather satellites. The backups continue the journey through balloons, auroras, and the instruments that make the invisible sky legible.

candidates.name: Mount Washington Observatory
candidates.why: Summit instruments, rime ice, fierce winds, weather archives, and a mountain mesonet offer a rugged ground-level beginning.

candidates.name: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory
candidates.why: Observatories and field campaigns track aerosols, ozone, radiation, and greenhouse gases, with calibration devices and sampling networks that could become atmospheric creatures.

candidates.name: EUMETSAT
candidates.why: Meteosat and Metop satellites, their sensors, orbits, ground systems, and images of ocean, land, and clouds carry the journey into space.

candidates.name: Malaysian Meteorological Department
candidates.why: Weather balloons and radiosondes, radar, monsoon observations, and marine forecasts make a richly inhabited tropical atmosphere.

candidates.name: University of Wisconsin Space Science and Engineering Center
candidates.why: Satellite imagery, atmospheric instruments, research projects, and weather visualization software offer many ways to see clouds from above.

candidates.name: University of Alaska Fairbanks Geophysical Institute
candidates.why: Auroras, atmospheric science, remote sensing, snow and ice, and research facilities connect the ground to the upper atmosphere.

candidates.name: Hong Kong Observatory
candidates.why: A coastal observatory with radar, tropical cyclone tracks, satellite imagery, weather records, and educational material on atmospheric phenomena.

candidates.name: Space Weather Prediction Center
candidates.why: Solar wind, auroras, geomagnetic disturbances, and observing spacecraft extend the weather journey beyond Earth's atmosphere.

candidates.name: National Weather Service
candidates.why: Radiosonde launches, Doppler radar, surface stations, forecasts, and weather education provide a deep reserve of sky-watching machinery and processes.
